findings.title: Failed 'Add entry' clears the text the user typed
findings.steps: Open a plant, type an entry, make POST /api/journal fail (500 or offline), click Add entry.
findings.expected: The error is shown and the typed text stays so the user can retry.
findings.actual: The error 'Could not add the entry.' shows but the textarea is emptied. addEntry calls entryForm.reset() in `finally`, so it runs on failure too.
findings.evidence: With POST mocked to 500, textarea value after submit was '' (it was 'My carefully typed note 🌱'). Alert: 'Could not add the entry.'

findings.title: Journal requests have no timeout; a hung save shows 'Saving…' forever
findings.steps: Make POST /api/journal hang (never respond) and click Add entry; wait more than 10 s.
findings.expected: The request fails after 10 s with a visible error and the button is enabled again.
findings.actual: The button still said 'Saving…' and stayed disabled after 13 s. No timeout is set on the $fetch client, so edit (PUT), delete and the GET lists hang the same way.
findings.evidence: Submit button text 'Saving…' 13 s after clicking with a hanging route.

findings.title: Journal page error state has no retry
findings.steps: Make GET /api/journal fail (503), go to the Journal page through the nav link.
findings.expected: An error message with a Retry button that reloads the list once the server is back.
findings.actual: Only 'Could not load the journal.' is shown. There is no retry button; the only ways to recover are a reload or changing the search text.
findings.evidence: Page text 'Could not load the journal.'; 0 buttons matching retry/try again.

findings.title: Plant detail journal load error has no retry
findings.steps: Make GET /api/journal?plant_id=... fail (500), open a plant from the Plants list.
findings.expected: The journal error offers a Retry that calls refreshJournal.
findings.actual: Only 'Could not load the journal.' is shown, with no retry control. The header badge still shows the count (e.g. '3 entries') next to an empty, failed list.
findings.evidence: Section text: 'Journal 3 entries ... Could not load the journal.'; no retry button.

findings.title: Huge plant_id / entry id gives 500 instead of 4xx
findings.steps: POST /api/journal with plant_id 99999999999999999999, or GET /api/journal?plant_id=99999999999999999999, or PUT /api/journal/99999999999999999999.
findings.actual: 500 Internal Server Error (SQLite integer overflow). The id fields have no upper bound.

findings.title: Journal page overflows sideways at 375 px with a long plant name
findings.steps: Create a plant named with 80 characters and no spaces (allowed by the API), add an entry, open /journal at 375 px wide.
findings.expected: No horizontal scrolling; the long name wraps.
findings.actual: document scrollWidth is 679 px against a 375 px viewport. The .journal-feed__plant link has no overflow-wrap, so the whole feed card widens.
findings.evidence: scrollWidth/clientWidth = 679/375; the overflowing elements are A.journal-feed__plant and its row (right edge 662 px).

findings.title: Search longer than 80 characters shows a raw validation message
findings.expected: The input limits the length, or a friendly message is shown.
findings.actual: The list is replaced by 'Query.q: String should have at most 80 characters'. The input has no maxlength.
findings.evidence: Page text after typing 100 'x': 'Query.q: String should have at most 80 characters'.

findings.title: Client limit counts UTF-16 units while the server counts characters
findings.steps: Type or paste 300 emoji into the entry.
findings.expected: 500 characters accepted, matching the server limit.
findings.actual: textarea maxlength=500 and form.body.length count UTF-16 code units, so emoji count double: only about 250 emoji fit and the counter is wrong.
findings.evidence: Code: :maxlength="BODY_LIMIT" and remaining = 500 - form.body.length; the server uses Python len (code points).

findings.title: Retrying a delete after a timeout or lost response shows an error
findings.steps: Delete an entry while the response is lost (the server deleted it), then click Delete again.
findings.expected: The second delete is treated as done (the entry is already gone).
findings.actual: The server returns 404 and the page shows 'Journal entry not found' instead of refreshing the list.
findings.evidence: delete_entry calls _get_entry first and raises 404; removeEntry shows the error without refreshing.
